types.embedding_query_text: Company: A commercial business organization that produces goods or services. Also called Corporation, Firm, Enterprise, Business. Examples: Meta, another company, the parent company of Facebook and Instagram, an unnamed company.

chosen_type.label: Corporation
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Company' directly matches schema.org's 'Corporation', which explicitly includes 'company' as an alternative name and fits the definition and mentions.

candidates.label: Corporation
candidates.comment: A Corporation is a legal entity separate from its owners, typically formed for business purposes. Also called company, incorporated business, limited company. Examples: Apple Inc., Google LLC, Microsoft Corporation, Coca-Cola Company. Distinct from Cooperative, which is an organization owned and operated by its members for their mutual benefit.

candidates.label: LocalBusiness
candidates.comment: A specific physical business or a branch of an organization that serves a local community. Also called local company, neighborhood business, regional enterprise. Examples: a local restaurant, a bank branch, a medical clinic, a bowling alley, a grocery store. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group of people with a particular purpose.

candidates.label: OnlineBusiness
candidates.comment: An OnlineBusiness is a particular business that operates primarily or entirely online. Also called e-business, internet business, digital enterprise. Examples: an e-commerce site, an online travel agency, a virtual doctor's office. Distinct from LocalBusiness, which has a physical presence.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SomeProducts
candidates.comment: A placeholder representing multiple similar products of the same kind, used when specific individual products are not distinguished. Also called product group, product category, generic products, similar items. Examples: 'a batch of apples', 'several identical t-shirts', 'a collection of standard screws'.

types.embedding_query_text: Date: A specific point in time, typically a day, month, and year. Also called Calendar date, Day, Specific date. Examples: 06/08/2026.

chosen_type.label: Date
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Date' and its definition perfectly align with schema.org's 'Date' datatype, which represents a specific calendar date.

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

types.embedding_query_text: SocialMediaCompany: A company that operates a social media platform or service. Also called Social network provider, Social platform company. Examples: Facebook, Instagram.

chosen_type.label: SocialMediaCorporation
chosen_type.definition: A corporation that operates a social media platform or service.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type specifically for a company operating social media platforms; 'Corporation' is the closest parent.

candidates.label: SocialMediaPosting
candidates.comment: A creative work published on a social media platform, such as a blog post, tweet, or Facebook update. Also called social post, microblog post, status update, online share. Examples: a tweet from a celebrity, a Facebook status update, a blog post on Medium, an Instagram caption.

candidates.label: DiscussionForumPosting
candidates.comment: A social media posting that is an entry or message within an online discussion forum. Also called Forum post, message board entry, thread reply, online discussion. Examples: A question posted on a tech support forum, a comment in a gaming community thread, a new topic started on a hobby board. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is typically a longer, standalone article on a blog.

candidates.label: MovingCompany
candidates.comment: A MovingCompany is a local business that provides services for relocating belongings. Also called relocation service, removal company, movers. Examples: U-Haul, Two Men and a Truck, local moving service. Distinct from HomeAndConstructionBusiness, which is a broader category for home-related services.

candidates.label: OnlineBusiness
candidates.comment: An OnlineBusiness is a particular business that operates primarily or entirely online. Also called e-business, internet business, digital enterprise. Examples: an e-commerce site, an online travel agency, a virtual doctor's office. Distinct from LocalBusiness, which has a physical presence.

candidates.label: BlogPosting
candidates.comment: An Article that is an individual entry or post published within a blog. Also called blog post, blog entry, weblog post. Examples: "A blog post about new software features", "An article on a travel blog", "A recipe post on a food blog". Distinct from Blog, which is the collection of posts.

types.embedding_query_text: Person: An individual human being. Also called Individual, Human, Agent. Examples: Meta spokesperson, source, Irregular spokesperson, a spokesperson.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Person' and its definition are a direct match for schema.org's 'Person'.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: ProfilePage
candidates.comment: A ProfilePage is a WebPage dedicated to displaying information about a specific entity, such as a person or organization. Also called user profile, personal page, bio page. Examples: a LinkedIn profile, a social media user's page, an author's biography page, a company's "About Us" page.

types.embedding_query_text: DayOfWeek: A named day in the seven-day cycle of a week. Also called Weekday, Weekend day. Examples: Wednesday.

chosen_type.label: DayOfWeek
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'DayOfWeek' and its definition are a direct match for schema.org's 'DayOfWeek' enumeration.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

types.embedding_query_text: TestingProcess: A systematic procedure or series of actions performed to evaluate the functionality, performance, or security of a system or product. Also called Evaluation process, Assessment, Trial. Examples: cybersecurity testing, testing of the model, evaluation, cyber evals.

chosen_type.label: CheckAction
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'TestingProcess' aligns well with 'CheckAction', which describes the act of inspecting or examining an object's condition, fitting 'cybersecurity testing'.

candidates.label: DiagnosticProcedure
candidates.comment: A medical procedure primarily performed to identify or confirm a disease or condition, rather than to treat it. Also called Medical test, diagnostic test, screening procedure, examination. Examples: MRI scan, blood test, biopsy, X-ray, colonoscopy. Distinct from TherapeuticProcedure, which is performed for treatment purposes.

candidates.label: CheckAction
candidates.comment: The act of an agent inspecting, investigating, or examining an object's accuracy, quality, or condition. Also called verify, inspect, examine, audit, review. Examples: Checking a document for errors, checking a car's oil level, checking a patient's vital signs.

candidates.label: AssessAction
candidates.comment: An AssessAction is an Action involving the formation of an opinion, reaction, or sentiment about something. Also called evaluate, appraise, judge, review, rate. Examples: a critic reviewing a movie, a teacher grading an assignment, a user rating a product, a doctor evaluating a patient's condition.

candidates.label: ReviewAction
candidates.comment: The act of an agent producing a balanced opinion about an object for an audience, resulting in a review. Also called assessing, evaluating, critiquing, giving feedback. Examples: a food critic writing about a new restaurant, a user submitting a product rating, a judge scoring a performance. Distinct from Review, which is the creative work itself, not the action of creating it.

candidates.label: SurgicalProcedure
candidates.comment: A medical procedure involving an incision with instruments, performed for diagnostic or therapeutic purposes. Also called surgery, operation, medical incision, surgical intervention. Examples: an appendectomy, a knee replacement surgery, a biopsy, a C-section.

types.embedding_query_text: AICompany: A company that specializes in the research, development, or application of artificial intelligence technologies. Also called Artificial intelligence firm, AI developer. Examples: OpenAI, Anthropic.

chosen_type.label: AICompany
chosen_type.definition: A company that specializes in the research, development, or application of artificial intelligence technologies.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type specifically for an AI company; 'Corporation' is the closest parent.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

candidates.label: MovingCompany
candidates.comment: A MovingCompany is a local business that provides services for relocating belongings. Also called relocation service, removal company, movers. Examples: U-Haul, Two Men and a Truck, local moving service. Distinct from HomeAndConstructionBusiness, which is a broader category for home-related services.

candidates.label: WebAPI
candidates.comment: An application programming interface that is accessible over web or internet technologies. Also called web service, API, REST API. Examples: the Google Maps API, the Twitter API, a weather data API.

candidates.label: APIReference
candidates.comment: APIReference, as a TechArticle under CreativeWork, provides documentation for application programming interfaces. Also called API documentation, developer reference, programming interface guide. Examples: Google Maps API documentation, Stripe API reference, Python `requests` library documentation.

candidates.label: NLNonprofitType
candidates.comment: NLNonprofitType is an enumeration for specific non-profit organization types originating from the Netherlands. Also called Dutch non-profit type, Netherlands charity classification. Examples: ANBI (Algemeen Nut Beogende Instelling), SBBI (Sociaal Belang Behartigende Instelling). Distinct from NonprofitType, which is a general enumeration for non-profit types.

types.embedding_query_text: TestingCompany: A company that provides services for testing products, systems, or software. Also called Quality assurance firm, QA company, Certification body. Examples: Irregular, an independent testing company Meta uses.

chosen_type.label: TestingCompany
chosen_type.definition: A company that provides services for testing products, systems, or software.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type specifically for a general testing company; 'Corporation' is the closest parent.

candidates.label: MedicalTest
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any medical test, typically performed for diagnostic purposes. Also called diagnostic test, clinical examination, medical screening. Examples: "blood test", "urine test", "MRI scan", "biopsy", "physical exam".

candidates.label: MedicalTestPanel
candidates.comment: A medical test that is a collection of tests commonly ordered together. Also called test battery, diagnostic panel, group of tests. Examples: "complete blood count (CBC)", "liver function panel", "metabolic panel". Distinct from MedicalTest, which can be a single test.

candidates.label: CovidTestingFacility
candidates.comment: A CovidTestingFacility is a medical clinic or other designated location where individuals can receive testing for the COVID-19 Coronavirus disease. Also called COVID test site, coronavirus testing center, SARS-CoV-2 testing facility. Examples: A drive-thru COVID testing center, a pharmacy offering COVID tests, a hospital's dedicated testing unit.

candidates.label: DiagnosticLab
candidates.comment: A medical organization that provides on-site or off-site diagnostic services, such as testing and analysis. Also called Medical laboratory, pathology lab, clinical lab, testing facility. Examples: Quest Diagnostics, LabCorp, a hospital's pathology department. Distinct from MedicalClinic, which provides direct patient care and consultations.

candidates.label: Certification
candidates.comment: An official and authoritative statement attesting to specific characteristics of a subject, issued by an independent body. Also called accreditation, credential, attestation, endorsement. Examples: ISO 9001 certification, Organic food certification, PMP certification, LEED certification.

types.embedding_query_text: ConfigurationError: A mistake or flaw in the setup or arrangement of a system or software. Also called Misconfiguration, Setup error, Setting mistake. Examples: misconfiguration, inadvertent error, issue in the setup.

chosen_type.label: Error
chosen_type.justification: A 'misconfiguration' is a type of 'Error' or problem, fitting the definition of a flaw in a system.

candidates.label: Error
candidates.comment: An Error is an InstantaneousEvent representing a problem or failure that occurred. Also called fault, malfunction, issue. Examples: A 404 Not Found error, a database connection error, a system crash, a data validation error.

candidates.label: CorrectionComment
candidates.comment: A CorrectionComment is a specific type of comment that provides corrections or amendments to a CreativeWork. Also called erratum, amendment, revision note. Examples: A correction notice on an online article, an errata sheet for a book, a revised caption for an image.

candidates.label: UserCheckins
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of checking into a location or event. Also called user check-in, location check-in, event attendance. Examples: a user checking into a restaurant, checking into a concert, marking attendance at a conference.

candidates.label: InstallAction
candidates.comment: An InstallAction is a consume action representing the act of installing an application or software. Also called set up action, deploy action, load software. Examples: installing a new app on a phone, setting up an operating system, deploying a server application.

candidates.label: ShippingRateSettings
candidates.comment: A structured value representing reusable shipping rate information, often linked to an offer via a shipping settings link. Also called shipping cost rules, freight pricing, delivery charges configuration. Examples: a flat rate shipping setting for standard delivery, a weight-based shipping rate table, a zone-based shipping cost.

types.embedding_query_text: Network: A system of interconnected computers or devices that can share resources and data. Also called Computer network, Data network, Web. Examples: internet, the open internet.

chosen_type.label: ComputerNetwork
chosen_type.definition: A system of interconnected computers or devices that can share resources and data.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type for a general computer network; 'Thing' is the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: InternetCafe
candidates.comment: An InternetCafe is a local business providing public access to computers with internet connectivity, often alongside food and beverages. Also called cyber cafe, web cafe, net cafe. Examples: a local internet cafe, a gaming cafe with internet access.

candidates.label: WebSite
candidates.comment: A collection of related web pages and other items, typically served from a single domain. Also called website, internet site, web presence. Examples: schema.org, Wikipedia, The New York Times website.

candidates.label: WebPage
candidates.comment: A single document or resource accessible via a web browser, typically part of a larger website. Also called web document, HTML page, internet page. Examples: a product page on an e-commerce site, a news article page, a contact us page.

candidates.label: Conversation
candidates.comment: A series of one or more messages exchanged between individuals or organizations on a specific topic. Also called discussion, dialogue, chat, discourse. Examples: An email thread, a text message exchange, a forum discussion, a spoken dialogue. Distinct from Comment, which is a single remark on an item.

candidates.label: GameServer
candidates.comment: A GameServer is an Intangible server that facilitates game interaction in a multiplayer game. Also called game host, multiplayer server. Examples: A dedicated server for an online game, a private game server for friends, a public game server for a large community.

types.embedding_query_text: AIModel: A software program or algorithm designed to perform tasks that typically require human intelligence, often trained on data. Also called Artificial intelligence algorithm, Machine learning model, AI agent. Examples: Muse Spark, AI models, Meta’s Muse Spark model, one of our models.

chosen_type.label: SoftwareApplication
chosen_type.justification: An AI model, being a program or algorithm designed to perform tasks, can be considered a specialized 'SoftwareApplication'.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

candidates.label: UserPlusOnes
candidates.comment: An outdated type representing a user's interaction of giving a "+1" endorsement, typically on Google+ or similar platforms. Also called user endorsement, +1, social recommendation. Examples: a user giving a +1 to a web page, endorsing a business, recommending content.

candidates.label: MathSolver
candidates.comment: A creative work that is a tool or application capable of solving a subset of mathematical problems. Also called mathematical calculator, problem solver, equation solver. Examples: an online algebra solver, a geometry calculator, a calculus problem-solving app.

candidates.label: SoftwareSourceCode
candidates.comment: The human-readable instructions written in a programming language that define a software application. Also called source code, program code, script, code snippet. Examples: Python script for data analysis, C++ code for a game engine, HTML/CSS/JavaScript for a website, a Java class file.

candidates.label: SolveMathAction
candidates.comment: The action of taking a mathematical expression and directing users to a resource capable of solving or simplifying it. Also called math solving, equation solving, calculation action. Examples: entering '2+2' into a calculator app, inputting a complex equation into Wolfram Alpha, using a math solver website.

types.embedding_query_text: SecurityVulnerability: A weakness or flaw in a system's security that can be exploited by attackers. Also called Security flaw, Weakness, Exploit. Examples: security vulnerability.

chosen_type.label: SecurityVulnerability
chosen_type.definition: A weakness or flaw in a system's security that can be exploited by attackers.
chosen_type.justification: No direct schema.org equivalent; 'MedicalRiskFactor' is conceptually similar but domain-specific. 'Thing' is the most appropriate general parent.

candidates.label: Error
candidates.comment: An Error is an InstantaneousEvent representing a problem or failure that occurred. Also called fault, malfunction, issue. Examples: A 404 Not Found error, a database connection error, a system crash, a data validation error.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

candidates.label: GameServer
candidates.comment: A GameServer is an Intangible server that facilitates game interaction in a multiplayer game. Also called game host, multiplayer server. Examples: A dedicated server for an online game, a private game server for friends, a public game server for a large community.

candidates.label: WarrantyPromise
candidates.comment: A structured value representing the duration and scope of free services provided for a product's defects or malfunctions. Also called product warranty, guarantee, service promise. Examples: a 1-year manufacturer's warranty, a 90-day repair guarantee, a lifetime parts warranty.

candidates.label: MedicalConditionStage
candidates.comment: A medical intangible representing a specific stage of a medical condition. Also called disease stage, condition phase, severity level. Examples: "Stage IIIa cancer", "early-stage Alzheimer's", "acute phase of an infection".

types.embedding_query_text: Document: A piece of written, printed, or electronic matter that provides information or evidence. Also called Report, Paper, Record, Text. Examples: statement, white paper, retrospective.

chosen_type.label: DigitalDocument
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Document' and its mentions ('statement', 'white paper', 'retrospective') are well-represented by 'DigitalDocument', as most modern documents are electronic.

candidates.label: DigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A creative work representing an electronic file or document. Also called Electronic document, e-document, digital file, computer file. Examples: A PDF report, a Word document, a spreadsheet, an image file, an e-book. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.

candidates.label: TextDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A digital document primarily composed of textual content. Also called text file, digital document, e-document. Examples: a PDF report, a Word document, an e-book. Distinct from TextObject, which is a media object representing a text file, often for embedding or linking.

candidates.label: Statement
candidates.comment: A declaration or assertion about something, often a fact or an interesting piece of information. Also called assertion, declaration, factoid, claim. Examples: 'The Earth is round', 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius', 'The capital of France is Paris'. Distinct from Claim, which is used for more formal, verifiable assertions in fact-checking.

candidates.label: NoteDigitalDocument
candidates.comment: A NoteDigitalDocument, as a DigitalDocument, is a file containing a note, primarily for the author's reference. Also called digital note, electronic memo, text note. Examples: a personal reminder in a digital format, a draft of an idea, a quick thought saved electronically. Distinct from BlogPosting, which is intended for public consumption.

candidates.label: Manuscript
candidates.comment: A creative work, such as a book, document, or musical piece, written by hand rather than typed or printed. Also called handwritten document, original script, autograph. Examples: a medieval illuminated manuscript, an author's handwritten draft of a novel, a composer's original musical score.

types.embedding_query_text: Week: A period of seven days. Also called Seven-day period. Examples: last week.

chosen_type.label: Week
chosen_type.definition: A period of seven consecutive days.
chosen_type.justification: No direct schema.org type for a 'Week'; 'Duration' is the most appropriate parent as it represents a period of time.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

types.embedding_query_text: Organization: A structured group of people with a particular purpose. Also called Institution, Association, Body. Examples: three different organizations.

chosen_type.label: Organization
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'Organization' and its definition are a direct match for schema.org's 'Organization'.

candidates.label: Organization
candidates.comment: An Organization is a group of people with a particular purpose, such as a school, NGO, corporation, or club. Also called entity, institution, association. Examples: Google, Harvard University, Red Cross, a local sports club. Distinct from Person, which is an individual.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: MedicalOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization, physical or virtual, operating in the medical domain, such as a hospital or clinic. Also called healthcare organization, medical institution, health system. Examples: "Mayo Clinic", "World Health Organization", "Doctors Without Borders". Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any group.

candidates.label: Consortium
candidates.comment: A membership organization typically composed of other organizations collaborating on a shared project or goal. Also called alliance, syndicate, federation, partnership. Examples: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), a research consortium, a banking consortium, a joint venture. Distinct from Organization, which is a general grouping of people or entities.

candidates.label: SearchRescueOrganization
candidates.comment: An organization dedicated to finding and providing aid to people who are lost or in imminent danger. Also called SAR team, rescue service, emergency search unit. Examples: a mountain rescue team, a coast guard search and rescue unit, a volunteer SAR group.

types.embedding_query_text: SecurityBreachType: A specific category or method of unauthorized access or data exposure. Also called Breach method, Attack vector, Exploitation type. Examples: sandbox escape.

chosen_type.label: SecurityBreachType
chosen_type.definition: A specific category or method of unauthorized access or data exposure.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type for a classification of security breaches; 'Enumeration' is the most appropriate parent for a type classification.

candidates.label: PaymentMethodType
candidates.comment: PaymentMethodType is an enumeration for generic types of payment methods. Also called payment category, payment classification. Examples: CreditCard, DebitCard, BankTransfer, Cash. Distinct from PaymentMethod, which can be a specific instance or a broader concept.

candidates.label: GovernmentBenefitsType
candidates.comment: GovernmentBenefitsType is an enumeration of various government benefits, particularly those related to supporting situations like COVID-19. Also called public assistance types, state aid categories, welfare program kinds. Examples: unemployment benefits, stimulus checks, housing assistance, food stamps.

candidates.label: MusicAlbumReleaseType
candidates.comment: MusicAlbumReleaseType is an enumeration describing the kind of release for a music album. Also called release format, album release category. Examples: Single, EP, Album. Distinct from MusicAlbumProductionType, which describes the content type.

candidates.label: DigitalDocumentPermissionType
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific type of permission that can be granted for accessing a digital document. Also called Access level, permission role, document access type. Examples: ReadPermission, WritePermission, SharePermission, CommentPermission. Distinct from DigitalDocumentPermission, which is an instance of a permission granted to a specific entity.

candidates.label: LoginAction
candidates.comment: The action of gaining access to a device or application by providing credentials. Also called sign in, log on, user authentication. Examples: logging into a website, signing into a mobile app, logging onto a computer. Distinct from ControlAction, which is a broader category for actions that control something.

types.embedding_query_text: CyberActionType: A classification of actions or activities performed in a cyber context, often with malicious intent. Also called Cyberattack type, Digital action, Online activity. Examples: sophisticated cyber action.

chosen_type.label: CyberActionType
chosen_type.definition: A classification of actions or activities performed in a cyber context, often with malicious intent.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type for a classification of cyber actions; 'Enumeration' is the most appropriate parent for a type classification.

candidates.label: ControlAction
candidates.comment: An action where an agent operates or manages a device or application. Also called controlling, operating, managing, manipulating. Examples: Turning on a light, adjusting a thermostat, launching a software application, steering a car. Distinct from Action, which is a general activity.

candidates.label: SearchAction
candidates.comment: The act of looking for an object or information, often using a search engine or database. Also called searching, querying, looking up, seeking. Examples: typing a query into Google, searching for a file on a computer, looking up a contact in a directory. Distinct from FindAction, which is the result of a search, not the act itself.

candidates.label: PlayGameAction
candidates.comment: PlayGameAction is a ConsumeAction specifically representing the act of playing a video game. Also called gaming, video gaming, playing a digital game. Examples: playing "Minecraft", playing "Fortnite", playing "Chess" online, playing a mobile game. Distinct from PlayAction, which is a broader act of playing or performing.

candidates.label: UseAction
candidates.comment: The act of applying an object to its intended purpose or function. Also called utilize, employ, operate. Examples: using a tool to fix something, consuming food, wearing clothes.

candidates.label: InteractAction
candidates.comment: An InteractAction is an action representing the act of interacting with another person or organization. Also called engagement action, social action, communication action. Examples: communicating, joining, inviting, following. Distinct from CommunicateAction, which is a specific type of interaction focused on information exchange.

types.embedding_query_text: Practice: A customary way of operating or doing things, often considered effective or standard. Also called Method, Procedure, Technique, Guideline. Examples: best practices.

chosen_type.label: BestPractice
chosen_type.definition: A customary way of operating or doing things, often considered effective or standard.
chosen_type.justification: No direct schema.org type for a general 'practice' or 'best practice'; 'Thing' is the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: MedicalGuidelineContraindication
candidates.comment: A medical guideline that specifically designates a process as harmful, supported by sound data. Also called contraindicated guideline, harmful practice warning, medical prohibition. Examples: "guideline against routine antibiotic use for viral infections", "contraindication for specific surgical techniques". Distinct from MedicalGuidelineRecommendation, which suggests an efficacious process.

candidates.label: MedicalGuidelineRecommendation
candidates.comment: A medical guideline that recommends a process as efficacious, supported by sound data. Also called recommended guideline, best practice recommendation, medical advice. Examples: "guideline recommending statins for high cholesterol", "recommendation for early cancer screening". Distinct from MedicalGuidelineContraindication, which warns against a harmful process.

candidates.label: UseAction
candidates.comment: The act of applying an object to its intended purpose or function. Also called utilize, employ, operate. Examples: using a tool to fix something, consuming food, wearing clothes.

candidates.label: SurgicalProcedure
candidates.comment: A medical procedure involving an incision with instruments, performed for diagnostic or therapeutic purposes. Also called surgery, operation, medical incision, surgical intervention. Examples: an appendectomy, a knee replacement surgery, a biopsy, a C-section.

candidates.label: Guide
candidates.comment: A Guide is a creative work that recommends specific products, services, or aspects of a thing for a user to consider, often detailing features or providing rankings. Also called buying guide, product review, ranked list, how-to manual. Examples: 'Best Laptops of 2023' article, a travel guide to Paris, a car buying guide, a beginner's photography guide. Distinct from HowTo, which provides step-by-step instructions to achieve a result.

types.embedding_query_text: SecurityMeasure: An action or device intended to prevent or detect unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification, or destruction of information. Also called Safeguard, Protection, Precaution. Examples: containment.

chosen_type.label: SecurityMeasure
chosen_type.definition: An action or precaution taken to prevent crime or ensure safety.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type for a general 'security measure'; 'Thing' is the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: AuthenticateAction
candidates.comment: An AuthenticateAction is a ControlAction representing the act of verifying one's identity to gain access to a device or application. Also called log in, sign in, verify identity, authorize access. Examples: logging into a website, unlocking a phone with a password, using a fingerprint scanner to access an app, authenticating with a two-factor code.

candidates.label: WarrantyScope
candidates.comment: An enumeration describing the range of services covered by a warranty in case of product defect or malfunction. Also called warranty coverage, guarantee scope, service level. Examples: "Parts and Labor - Bring In", "Labor - On Site", "Parts Only".

candidates.label: LoginAction
candidates.comment: The action of gaining access to a device or application by providing credentials. Also called sign in, log on, user authentication. Examples: logging into a website, signing into a mobile app, logging onto a computer. Distinct from ControlAction, which is a broader category for actions that control something.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskEstimator
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any rule set or interactive tool used to estimate the risk of developing a complication or condition. Also called risk assessment tool, prognosis predictor, clinical risk model. Examples: a calculator for stroke risk, a scoring system for surgical complications. Distinct from MedicalRiskFactor, which is a single factor increasing risk.

candidates.label: SuspendAction
candidates.comment: The act of momentarily pausing a device, application, or process. Also called pausing, halting, putting on hold, temporarily stopping. Examples: pausing music playback, suspending a computer process, pausing a timer.

types.embedding_query_text: NewsOrganization: A company or entity responsible for gathering, producing, and disseminating news and information. Also called Media outlet, News agency, Publisher. Examples: The Information, CNN.

chosen_type.label: NewsMediaOrganization
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'NewsOrganization' and its definition are a direct match for schema.org's 'NewsMediaOrganization'.

candidates.label: NewsMediaOrganization
candidates.comment: A NewsMediaOrganization is an organization that produces and disseminates news, such as a newspaper or TV station. Also called news agency, media outlet, journalistic organization. Examples: The New York Times, BBC News, CNN. Distinct from Organization, which is a broader category for any type of organization.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

candidates.label: ArchiveOrganization
candidates.comment: An ArchiveOrganization is a LocalBusiness that maintains, preserves, and typically provides public access to archival materials. Also called archives, historical society, records center, repository. Examples: National Archives, a university special collections library, a corporate archive, a local historical society.

candidates.label: GovernmentOrganization
candidates.comment: A GovernmentOrganization is an organization or agency that is part of a governmental body. Also called public sector entity, state agency, governmental body. Examples: Department of Defense, Environmental Protection Agency, National Institutes of Health, local city council.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

types.embedding_query_text: ComputerSystem: A complete, working computer, including hardware, software, and peripheral equipment, used for processing data. Also called IT system, Computing system, Digital system. Examples: internal system.

chosen_type.label: ComputerSystem
chosen_type.definition: A complete, working computer, including hardware, software, and peripheral equipment, used for processing data.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type for a general 'computer system'; 'Thing' is the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: OperatingSystem
candidates.comment: An OperatingSystem, as a SoftwareApplication, is system software that manages computer hardware and software resources. Also called OS, system software, platform. Examples: Windows, macOS, Linux, Android. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is a general application program.

candidates.label: ComputerStore
candidates.comment: A local business specializing in the retail sale of computers and related equipment. Also called PC store, electronics store, computer shop. Examples: Best Buy, Apple Store, a local computer repair and sales shop, Micro Center. Distinct from Store, which is a general retail establishment.

candidates.label: MedicineSystem
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing different systems of medical practice. Also called healthcare system, medical tradition, healing approach. Examples: "WesternConventional", "Ayurvedic", "TraditionalChineseMedicine", "Homeopathic".

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

candidates.label: ComputerLanguage
candidates.comment: A formal language used for computer programming or other computer representations. Also called programming language, coding language, machine language. Examples: Python, Java, C++, SQL, HTML, XML. Distinct from Language, which refers to natural human languages.

types.embedding_query_text: TestingEnvironment: A setup or configuration of hardware, software, and network resources used for testing purposes. Also called Testbed, Sandbox, Development environment. Examples: testing environments.

chosen_type.label: TestingEnvironment
chosen_type.definition: A setup or configuration of hardware, software, and network resources used for testing purposes.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type for a general 'testing environment'; 'Thing' is the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: RuntimePlatform
candidates.comment: A specialized software environment providing the necessary infrastructure, libraries, and services for executing a program. Also called execution environment, software platform, runtime environment, operating system. Examples: Java Virtual Machine (JVM), Node.js runtime, .NET Common Language Runtime (CLR), Python interpreter.

candidates.label: DigitalPlatformEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration listing common technology platforms, used to specify where an action or content is available. Also called Technology platform, software platform, operating system, device type. Examples: iOS, Android, Web, Desktop, Console. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is the application itself, not the platform it runs on.

candidates.label: CampingPitch
candidates.comment: An individual outdoor space for overnight stay, typically part of a larger camping site or campground. Also called tent pitch, RV pitch, caravan pitch, campsite spot. Examples: Tent site #3 at Yosemite, RV spot at KOA, a designated area for a caravan. Distinct from Campground, which is the larger site containing multiple pitches.

candidates.label: CovidTestingFacility
candidates.comment: A CovidTestingFacility is a medical clinic or other designated location where individuals can receive testing for the COVID-19 Coronavirus disease. Also called COVID test site, coronavirus testing center, SARS-CoV-2 testing facility. Examples: A drive-thru COVID testing center, a pharmacy offering COVID tests, a hospital's dedicated testing unit.

candidates.label: MedicalTest
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any medical test, typically performed for diagnostic purposes. Also called diagnostic test, clinical examination, medical screening. Examples: "blood test", "urine test", "MRI scan", "biopsy", "physical exam".

types.embedding_query_text: ThreatScenario: A hypothetical situation describing a potential threat or risk, often used for planning and testing. Also called Risk scenario, Threat model, Attack scenario. Examples: real world threat scenarios.

chosen_type.label: ThreatScenario
chosen_type.definition: A hypothetical situation describing a potential threat or risk, often used for planning and testing.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type for a 'threat scenario'; 'Thing' is the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskEstimator
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any rule set or interactive tool used to estimate the risk of developing a complication or condition. Also called risk assessment tool, prognosis predictor, clinical risk model. Examples: a calculator for stroke risk, a scoring system for surgical complications. Distinct from MedicalRiskFactor, which is a single factor increasing risk.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskCalculator
candidates.comment: A medical risk estimator that is a complex mathematical calculation, often requiring an online tool, used to assess prognosis. Also called prognosis calculator, risk assessment tool, clinical prediction model. Examples: a calculator for cardiovascular disease risk, a tool for predicting cancer recurrence. Distinct from MedicalRiskScore, which is a simpler sum of risk factors.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

candidates.label: MemberProgramTier
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a specific tier within a loyalty or membership program. Also called membership level, loyalty tier, program status. Examples: "Gold Member", "Platinum Tier", "Basic Membership Level".

candidates.label: StadiumOrArena
candidates.comment: A large civic structure designed for sporting events, concerts, or other large-scale public gatherings. Also called stadium, arena, coliseum, sports complex. Examples: Wembley Stadium, Madison Square Garden, the Roman Colosseum.

types.embedding_query_text: Capability: The ability or power to do something. Also called Capacity, Ability, Competence. Examples: advanced capabilities, so much more capable.

chosen_type.label: Capability
chosen_type.definition: The ability or power to do something.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type for 'capability'; 'Thing' is the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: Role
candidates.comment: Additional information describing a relationship or property, such as a person's function in an organization or a character played in a movie. Also called function, capacity, position, part. Examples: 'actor' role for a person in a film, 'member' role for a player on a sports team, 'author' role for a person on a book.

candidates.label: ActionAccessSpecification
candidates.comment: An ActionAccessSpecification is an Intangible item detailing the requirements that must be met to perform a specific Action. Also called access requirements, action prerequisites, permission rules. Examples: "Requires login," "Subscription needed," "Age 18+," "Admin privileges."

candidates.label: Permit
candidates.comment: A Permit is an intangible entity representing an official authorization issued by an organization. Also called license, authorization, pass. Examples: a building permit, a parking permit, a fishing license. Distinct from LegalService, which is a service, not the document itself.

candidates.label: Service
candidates.comment: An intangible offering provided by an organization, such as delivery, consulting, or repair. Also called offering, provision, assistance, support. Examples: a car repair service, a legal consulting service, a package delivery service, a web hosting service.

candidates.label: MemberProgramTier
candidates.comment: An intangible representing a specific tier within a loyalty or membership program. Also called membership level, loyalty tier, program status. Examples: "Gold Member", "Platinum Tier", "Basic Membership Level".

types.embedding_query_text: Danger: The possibility of suffering harm or injury. Also called Risk, Hazard, Peril. Examples: potential dangers.

chosen_type.label: Risk
chosen_type.definition: A situation involving exposure to danger, harm, or loss.
chosen_type.justification: No direct schema.org type for a general 'danger' or 'risk'; 'MedicalRiskFactor' is too domain-specific. 'Thing' is the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskFactor
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing anything that increases a person's likelihood of developing a disease, medical condition, or complication. Also called risk element, predisposing factor, vulnerability. Examples: "smoking", "high cholesterol", "family history of heart disease", "obesity". Distinct from MedicalRiskEstimator, which is a tool to calculate risk based on multiple factors.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskEstimator
candidates.comment: A medical entity representing any rule set or interactive tool used to estimate the risk of developing a complication or condition. Also called risk assessment tool, prognosis predictor, clinical risk model. Examples: a calculator for stroke risk, a scoring system for surgical complications. Distinct from MedicalRiskFactor, which is a single factor increasing risk.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskCalculator
candidates.comment: A medical risk estimator that is a complex mathematical calculation, often requiring an online tool, used to assess prognosis. Also called prognosis calculator, risk assessment tool, clinical prediction model. Examples: a calculator for cardiovascular disease risk, a tool for predicting cancer recurrence. Distinct from MedicalRiskScore, which is a simpler sum of risk factors.

candidates.label: LoseAction
candidates.comment: The act of being defeated in a competitive activity or contest. Also called suffer defeat, be beaten, fail to win. Examples: losing a game, being defeated in an election, failing a competition. Distinct from AchieveAction, which is a broader category for actions that result in an outcome.

candidates.label: PreventionIndication
candidates.comment: A PreventionIndication is a MedicalIndication for preventing an underlying medical condition, symptom, or disease. Also called prophylactic indication, preventative use. Examples: a vaccine for measles prevention, a medication to prevent migraines, dietary changes to prevent heart disease, exercise to prevent diabetes.

types.embedding_query_text: TimePeriod: A duration or interval of time. Also called Period, Duration, Interval. Examples: few weeks.

chosen_type.label: Duration
chosen_type.definition: The length of time that something continues or lasts.
chosen_type.justification: The OIE type 'TimePeriod' and its definition are a direct match for schema.org's 'Duration', which represents a period of time.

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

candidates.label: TVSeason
candidates.comment: A distinct period of a television series, comprising multiple episodes, dedicated to TV broadcast and associated online delivery. Also called television season, broadcast season, show season. Examples: 'Season 1 of The Crown', 'The final season of Breaking Bad'. Distinct from Season, which is a more general media season.

types.embedding_query_text: Rank: A position in a hierarchy or a measure of importance or achievement. Also called Position, Standing, Order. Examples: third major AI company.

chosen_type.label: Rank
chosen_type.definition: A position in a hierarchy or a scale of quality or importance.
chosen_type.justification: No direct schema.org type for 'rank'; 'Rating' is a specific type of evaluation, not the general concept of rank. 'Thing' is the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: OrderStatus
candidates.comment: OrderStatus is an enumeration for the status values of an Order. Also called order state, delivery status, fulfillment status. Examples: OrderProcessing, OrderDelivered, OrderCancelled, OrderProblem. Distinct from PaymentStatusType, which describes the payment's state.

candidates.label: TierBenefitEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration of specific benefits offered as part of a loyalty or membership program. Also called loyalty program benefit, membership perk, reward tier. Examples: free shipping, early access to sales, exclusive content, dedicated customer support.

candidates.label: Order
candidates.comment: An Order is an intangible entity representing a confirmation of a transaction, containing accepted offers as line items. Also called purchase order, sales order, receipt. Examples: an online shopping order confirmation, a restaurant bill, a service agreement. Distinct from Offer, which is a proposal before acceptance.

candidates.label: ItemList
candidates.comment: An ItemList is an intangible collection of items of any sort, often ordered or ranked. Also called list, collection, sequence, array. Examples: 'Top 10 Movies,' a shopping list, a playlist, a table of contents. Distinct from ListItem, which is a single entry within an ItemList.

candidates.label: Rating
candidates.comment: A Rating is an Intangible representing an evaluation on a numeric scale, such as 1 to 5 stars. Also called score, grade, review rating. Examples: a 4-star movie rating, a product's 8/10 score, a customer satisfaction rating of 5 out of 5, a restaurant's health inspection grade.

types.embedding_query_text: Concept: An abstract idea or general notion. Also called Idea, Notion, Principle. Examples: mistakes.

chosen_type.label: Concept
chosen_type.definition: An abstract idea or general notion.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type for a general 'concept'; 'Error' is too narrow for the OIE type. 'Thing' is the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: Claim
candidates.comment: A specific, factually-oriented statement that can be reviewed for accuracy. Also called assertion, statement, proposition, contention. Examples: "The Earth is flat," "Coffee cures cancer," "This product is 100% organic." Distinct from ClaimReview, which is the review of a claim.

candidates.label: Statement
candidates.comment: A declaration or assertion about something, often a fact or an interesting piece of information. Also called assertion, declaration, factoid, claim. Examples: 'The Earth is round', 'Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius', 'The capital of France is Paris'. Distinct from Claim, which is used for more formal, verifiable assertions in fact-checking.

candidates.label: Error
candidates.comment: An Error is an InstantaneousEvent representing a problem or failure that occurred. Also called fault, malfunction, issue. Examples: A 404 Not Found error, a database connection error, a system crash, a data validation error.

candidates.label: CancelAction
candidates.comment: The act of asserting that a future event or action will no longer occur. Also called call off, revoke, annul, abort. Examples: Cancelling a flight, cancelling a meeting, cancelling a subscription. Distinct from ConfirmAction, which is asserting an event will happen.

candidates.label: CorrectionComment
candidates.comment: A CorrectionComment is a specific type of comment that provides corrections or amendments to a CreativeWork. Also called erratum, amendment, revision note. Examples: A correction notice on an online article, an errata sheet for a book, a revised caption for an image.

types.embedding_query_text: Standard: A level of quality or attainment. Also called Benchmark, Criterion, Norm. Examples: higher standards, up the standards significantly.

chosen_type.label: Standard
chosen_type.definition: A level of quality or attainment.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type for a general 'standard'; 'PropertyValueSpecification' is too specific. 'Thing' is the most appropriate parent.

candidates.label: Certification
candidates.comment: An official and authoritative statement attesting to specific characteristics of a subject, issued by an independent body. Also called accreditation, credential, attestation, endorsement. Examples: ISO 9001 certification, Organic food certification, PMP certification, LEED certification.

candidates.label: UnitPriceSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value detailing the price asked for a specific offer by an organization or person. Also called price details, cost specification, offer price. Examples: "$10.99 per item", "€50 per hour", "£2.50 per unit".

candidates.label: LegalValueLevel
candidates.comment: LegalValueLevel is an enumeration of possible levels for the legal validity or authority of a legislation. Also called legislative authority level, legal hierarchy, law's binding power. Examples: 'Primary', 'Secondary', 'Tertiary', 'Advisory'.

candidates.label: PropertyValueSpecification
candidates.comment: A PropertyValueSpecification is an Intangible defining the specification for a property's value. Also called value constraint, property definition. Examples: a specification for the allowed range of a numerical property, a definition of valid input for a text field, a schema for a complex property value.

candidates.label: MedicalEvidenceLevel
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing the level of evidence supporting a medical guideline. Also called evidence strength, guideline reliability, data quality level. Examples: "Level A evidence", "Grade 1 recommendation", "strong evidence".

types.embedding_query_text: Quality: A distinguishing characteristic or attribute. Also called Attribute, Characteristic, Feature. Examples: more complex, so much more complex.

chosen_type.label: PropertyValue
chosen_type.justification: A 'Quality' is a distinguishing characteristic or attribute, which is well-represented by 'PropertyValue' as a property-value pair.

candidates.label: LocationFeatureSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value that specifies a feature of an accommodation, represented as a property-value pair. Also called accommodation feature, amenity detail, property value specification. Examples: "hasWifi: true", "numberOfBedrooms: 3", "petsAllowed: false", "poolType: outdoor".

candidates.label: PropertyValue
candidates.comment: A PropertyValue is a StructuredValue representing a property-value pair, such as a feature of a product or place. Also called feature, attribute value, characteristic. Examples: "color: red", "weight: 5kg", "hasWifi: true", "engineType: V8". Distinct from using specific schema.org properties directly, which is preferred when available.

candidates.label: StructuredValue
candidates.comment: A value for a property that has a complex internal structure rather than being a simple text or reference. Also called complex data type, composite value, structured data. Examples: an address object with street, city, and zip code; a price specification with amount and currency; a time range with start and end times.

candidates.label: Property
candidates.comment: A Property is an Intangible used to indicate attributes and relationships of some Thing, equivalent to rdf:Property. Also called attribute, characteristic, relation. Examples: "name", "description", "url", "author".

candidates.label: UnitPriceSpecification
candidates.comment: A structured value detailing the price asked for a specific offer by an organization or person. Also called price details, cost specification, offer price. Examples: "$10.99 per item", "€50 per hour", "£2.50 per unit".
